clue.text: Needlework more than enough to occupy sister

indicators.note: the generous amount moves in and takes up residence within the sister abbreviation

parts.note: ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A nun's embroidery projects are so plentiful they fill her whole day.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampler is a piece of embroidery stitched to show off a range of stitches, so it is an example of needlework.

clue.text: Working men in drink get tight

indicators.note: in places the workers inside the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a crew is a team of men working together

explanation.surface: Labourers in the pub end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'get tight' suggests getting drunk; in the answer it means to tense up or tighten.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up one's face or eyes is to tense and tighten them.

clue.text: Materials processed in plant

indicators.note: processed means the letters are put through a mill and come out reordered

explanation.surface: Raw materials are handled in an industrial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory but is the green kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's tail is an aquatic perennial with whorled leaves, a flowering species.

clue.text: Old French coin laid very oddly on top of escritoire

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first part sits on the second, above it
oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters of each of the two words

parts.note: its odd letters, first and third, are taken
its odd letters, first and third, are taken

indicators.note: top of takes the uppermost, first letter of the writing desk word

parts.note: an escritoire is a writing desk; only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: An antique coin was placed carefully on a writing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: An escritoire is a writing desk.
explanation.definitionFit: The livre was the currency of France before the franc.

clue.text: Look back on cars: extremely comfortable

parts.note: re means on or concerning
Minis are small British cars

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone recalls cars that were wonderfully comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a classic small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past events fondly, looking back on them.

clue.text: Berated crazy speaker

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of the word before it have gone wild and are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone tells off an unhinged orator.
explanation.definitionFit: A debater is one who argues a motion aloud in public, a kind of speaker.

clue.text: One offering free kebab, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, matching another spelling

parts.note: a doner kebab is spit-roasted meat; doner is the word heard

explanation.surface: A takeaway hands out a kebab without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: A doner kebab is meat cut from a rotating spit.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives something, such as blood or money, without payment.

clue.text: Bird (black) wandering about

parts.note: B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black
rambling means roaming aimlessly

explanation.surface: A dark bird roams around.
explanation.definitionFit: The brambling is a finch related to the chaffinch, a winter visitor to Britain.

clue.text: Feeble golf is an obsession

parts.note: a thin excuse is a feeble one
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A weak game of golf becomes a fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to be fixated on it, an obsession.

clue.text: Lawyer confused about old special plural

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for old
confused means the letters of the lawyer word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A muddled lawyer talks about an old grammatical form.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal 'we' is the monarch speaking of themselves in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the plural pronoun used by a sovereign to mean the single speaker, a special use of the plural.

clue.text: Title of Sir Trevor not used in full

indicators.note: only part of the two words is taken, a run of letters lying across them

explanation.surface: A knight named Trevor is addressed without his full honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: RT REV abbreviates Right Reverend, the form of address for a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Right Reverend is the honorific placed before a bishop's name, a formal style of address.

clue.text: Deceit to get a financial centre working again

parts.note: to mend something is to get it working again
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Fraud is the price of reviving a moribund banking hub.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the square mile of London that houses its banks and markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacity is habitual lying, a synonym of deceit.

clue.text: Maybe American partners at table less easy-going

parts.note: at the bridge table West and East are partners, giving W and E
sterner means stricter, less relaxed

explanation.surface: American card partners are stricter than their opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, and West partners East.
explanation.definitionFit: An American is an example of a Westerner, someone from the western world.

clue.text: Seeing roll, one jokingly pulled sailor back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the combined pieces from end to start

parts.note: to pull someone's leg is to tease them
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: Someone sees a bread roll after teasing a seaman, who is pulled backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked.

clue.text: Parking where taxis do for a lark

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
taxis wait at a rank, and to rank is to line up there

explanation.surface: Someone parks in the taxi bay just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: A taxi rank is a place where cabs queue for passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of mischievous fun, the same as a prank or practical joke.

clue.text: One's precariously balanced here on side of cutter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a precarious, finely balanced situation
second meaning: the sharp edge of a blade

explanation.walkthrough: Being on a knife-edge means being in a tense, finely balanced position.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the sharp side of a blade and a perilously uncertain state.

clue.text: Feeling dreadfully intense before church

indicators.note: before places the jumbled part ahead of the church abbreviation
dreadfully suggests the word intense is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone feels terribly worked up before going to a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity for sensation, the ability to feel.

clue.text: Our French colleague? Hardly

parts.note: notre is French for our
an ally is a partner or colleague

explanation.surface: Is our French co-worker really one? Scarcely.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying not really expresses that something is scarcely or barely the case.

clue.text: Deductions come to this positive result: catch academic at it

definitions.text: Deductions come to this positive result

parts.note: to net is to catch
prof is short for professor, an academic

explanation.surface: Catch the professor in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Net profit is the gain left after costs and taxes have been subtracted from revenue.

clue.text: Girl worth €0.00001?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., a thousandth of a cent

explanation.walkthrough: A cent is a hundredth of a euro and milli- means a thousandth, so a millicent is a hundred-thousandth of a euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Millicent is a traditional female first name, as well as a jokey metric coin.

clue.text: More ink spilled fixing name

indicators.note: spilled suggests the letters splash out and land in a new order

explanation.surface: More ink has been spilt while writing a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Moniker is informal for a name or nickname.

clue.text: Billionaire has these guarding his entrance?

definitions.text: Billionaire has these guarding his entrance?

parts.words: Billionaire has these guarding his entrance?
parts.note: a rich man's driveway has barriers at the entrance; the Microsoft founder bears that very surname

explanation.walkthrough: Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft, is a billionaire; the barriers at his estate entrance share his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinged barriers closing an entrance, as well as the surname of the software tycoon.

clue.text: Defiant remark, angry about article

indicators.note: about means the word for angry goes round the article

parts.note: sore means annoyed or angry
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An angry person makes a defiant comment about a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: So there is a childish retort of defiance or triumph.

clue.text: A little reminder, for example, to ask repeatedly for money back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the pieces from right to left

parts.note: EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
to dun is to press a debtor for payment

explanation.surface: A debt collector sends a gentle prompt to someone who owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle prod or hint, a small prompt to remember something.

clue.text: Shoots game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moves or flies swiftly, as an arrow does
second meaning: the pub game of throwing at a board

explanation.walkthrough: Shoots means dashes, not fires or sprouts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means rushes swiftly and is also the board game played in pubs.

clue.text: Have a nose for trouble?

parts.note: to sense something is wrong, put as if literally sniffing out a problem

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to suspect deception, and the clue reads it as having a keen nose for wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sense that something is suspicious, detecting trouble as if by scent.

clue.text: Just over half moulded to the body? That's very poor

indicators.note: just over half means only five of the nine letters are kept, from the front

parts.note: skintight describes clothes clinging closely to the body

explanation.surface: A garment that is only half figure-hugging is a poor one.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for broke, with no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skint means having no money, being very poor.

clue.text: Gain access using emblem and name

parts.note: a logo is an emblem or symbol

explanation.surface: Someone gets into a system with a symbol and a username.
explanation.definitionFit: To log on is to enter a computer system, gaining entry with credentials.

clue.text: A contribution to road safety, one digging up part of the pavement?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the routine taught to British children for crossing the road

definitions.text: one digging up part of the pavement?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read literally, a drill that breaks up the kerb

explanation.walkthrough: Kerb drill was the British road safety routine of stopping at the kerb and looking both ways; a kerb is the edge of the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The routine was taught to schoolchildren to make crossing streets safer.

clue.text: Mistake supplying energy to house

indicators.note: supplying energy to the house means the energy letter is added on at its end

parts.note: gaff is British slang for a house or home
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An error in connecting power to a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaff is British slang for someone's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing error.

clue.text: Considerately treat muscle during inactivity

indicators.note: during places the muscle within the period of inactivity

parts.note: rest is a state of inactivity
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: A physio gently handles a strained muscle while the patient rests.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to show them due regard, treating them with consideration.

clue.text: Zany, get splashing in river

indicators.note: splashing suggests the letters are thrown about in disorder

explanation.surface: A wild person gets splashing about in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's longest waterway, flowing to the East China Sea.
